paper.title_en: Precision Calibration and Cosmic Birefringence with Simons Observatory
paper.abstract_en: <p>Precision cosmology experiments are ushering in an exciting era for fundamental physics by enabling searches for physics beyond the Standard Model and probing the extreme energy scales of the early Universe. Science cases such as identifying viable dark matter candidates, applying tighter constraints on the effective number of light relativistic species, and constraining cosmic birefringence are enabled by the deployment of increasingly sensitive Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) survey experiments like the Simons Observatory (SO). As experiments rapidly achieve large gains in sensitivity, the resolving factors of these ambitious science goals shift to the instrument&rsquo;s absolute calibrations such as its passbands and polarization angle.</p><p>In the first part of this thesis, I design, develop, and validate a novel bandpass calibrator with power variability that is capable of finely resolving bandpass edges. I then present material characterization of metamaterial anti-reflection cuttings and iron-loaded absorptive neutral density filters with varying concentrations that enable an extensive suite of in-lab testing and the necessary spectral corrections. This in-lab testing program is covered in the following chapter where we discuss the testing and integration of an SO small aperture telescope that housed a large aperture telescope&rsquo;s optics tube (&ldquo;camera&rdquo;). We fully populated the optical stack and carried out a range of testing to characterize and mitigate instrument systematics.</p><p>Finally, I discuss my work developing and fielding a bandpass calibrator for the SO small aperture telescopes. &nbsp;I design crossed-Dragonne style coupling optics and implement a mechanized design that permits scans over the full field-of-view of the telescope. Following in-lab testing and integration of the calibrator, we deploy it to the site and measure detector passbands. We confirm broad focal plane coverage and present preliminary passbands. We also offer a characterization of the SO small aperture telescope's polarization modulating half-wave plate's frequency dependence using these passbands. Future investigations are required to resolve a discrepancy with the expected performance. The half-wave plate's frequency dependent phase shift along with the passbands are necessary to properly calibrate the instrument's polarization angle for applications toward a probe of the parity-violating cosmic birefringence rotation angle, which is otherwise degenerate with the instrument's miscalibration angle.</p>
